manifesto_subtitle: Thirteen principles to honour the social fabric, memory, and future of our city.
manifesto_1_body:
A dense, ravishing city with deep cultural roots and a pressing need to reinvent itself. Its people have done so before, time and again—turning constraint into character, density into diversity, harbour into home.
SaanSeoi is our contribution to that future.
manifesto_2_body: Hong Kong changes fast enough to forget itself. The record of what was is inseparable from any account of what is—patterns of change, loss, and renewal only become legible across time. Official datasets have blind spots; community knowledge fills them. We hold both with care, treating the past as essential infrastructure.
manifesto_3_body: Every dataset encodes choices—what to measure, what to name, who to count. Geospatial data is especially loaded: it fixes boundaries, asserts presence, and renders others invisible. We build with that awareness, and stay honest about the trade-offs.
manifesto_4_lead: Social fabric is the core weave
manifesto_4_body:
A map of Hong Kong without its people is just geometry. The social fabric that makes this city pulse exists because of the bonds, trust, and restless energy accumulated over generations. Technology that erodes that fabric in the name of efficiency is a regression.
We build to strengthen the weave.
manifesto_5_body: The tools we adopt shape our attention, our relationships, our sense of place. We choose systems that amplify <u>curiosity</u>, <u>care</u>, and <u>collective capacity</u>—a trinity to strengthen the weave. But no local effort is insulated from the systems it sits within.
manifesto_6_body: The open web was captured by a handful of platforms. Our societies are still reckoning with the harm this concentration caused. This state is not final. We use the digital commons as the staging site for our intervention: to reseed agency with the people the internet was meant for.
manifesto_7_body: Every advancement builds on what came before. The digital commons is the save state of that effort in the digital realm—a shared inheritance, free for all to build upon. But inheritance only has value if it can be accessed.
manifesto_8_body: When data is locked behind expertise, paywalls, or needless complexity, that virtuous cycle of advancement is broken. What is gained in private value is lost in civic, social, and cultural capital. The barrier to entry should be as close to zero as possible.
manifesto_9_body: Open standards and shared foundations let efforts compound. When systems talk to each other, everyone builds forward instead of starting over.
manifesto_10_body: A startup routing deliveries, a journalist mapping neighborhood change, an artist visualising air quality—these users validate the commons more than any scale metric. The city is best understood at the scale it is lived in.
manifesto_11_body: The model where open data producers and consumers are strangers needs a reset. We treat data work as care work. The invisible parts (speccing, compilation, validation) are now informed by visible ones (outreach, facilitation, tending). This bridges the last mile from data to application, and keeps effort focused where it matters.
manifesto_12_body: Everything we create encodes a choice—what to prioritise, what to preserve, who to serve. We make those choices with the community we build for, and answer to it when we get them wrong. There is no neutral position. The only question is whether the choices are made with care, in public, and in service of the city.
manifesto_13_body:
The next few years will determine whether global developments enrich or erase the city we live in. That outcome isn't settled by policy or platforms alone—it's steered by what gets built at street level, by people who know what's at stake.
So we show up, and we build.

tiles_getting_started_description: Add SaanSeoi’s vector basemap to a web map, prototype, or service. Start with an account and API key, then exchange the key on your server for a short-lived tile token.
tiles_getting_started_step_one_body: Create a SaanSeoi account, or sign in if you already have one. It is where you manage access to your applications.
tiles_getting_started_step_two_body: In API keys, create one key for this application and save it somewhere secure. Give every application its own key so it can be revoked independently.
tiles_getting_started_step_three_body: MapLibre is a natural fit. Mapbox GL JS and any client with a request hook can use the same TileJSON endpoint and bearer header.
tiles_getting_started_exchange_heading: Mint a tile token on your server
tiles_getting_started_exchange_intro_bef: Your server sends the API key to
tiles_getting_started_exchange_intro_aft: audience. The response contains a bearer token valid for 15 minutes.
tiles_getting_started_exchange_browser: Give the browser a fresh bearer token through your own application endpoint. Do not let a shared cache store that response.
tiles_getting_started_add_basemap_headin: Pass the bearer token to every SaanSeoi tile request.
tiles_getting_started_add_basemap_intro_: is the Hong Kong TileJSON endpoint. It tells your map library where to fetch the vector tiles. Use your own style layers for the source, or adapt a compatible Protomaps style.
tiles_getting_started_maplibre_descripti: Recommended for an open-source, Mapbox-style-compatible web map. Its
hook applies the header to TileJSON and tile requests.
tiles_getting_started_mapbox_description: Keep your Mapbox public token separate. The SaanSeoi bearer token belongs only on requests to the SaanSeoi tile origin.
tiles_getting_started_other_libraries_de: For OpenLayers, Leaflet vector-tile plugins, native apps, and custom renderers, use the library’s tile-load or request hook. If it cannot send headers, proxy tile requests through your server.
tiles_getting_started_account_body: Your human sign-in and the home for your API keys. Never use your account session as a map credential.
tiles_getting_started_api_key_body: A long-lived secret for your application. Send it only from trusted server-side code to mint a token. Never expose it to browsers, users, source control, or logs.
tiles_getting_started_bearer_token_body: A short-lived, tiles-only credential. It may be delivered to a browser that is loading your map, but treat it as sensitive: do not publish, log, or share it. Refresh it before it expires.
tiles_getting_started_security_note_befo: A browser-based integration also needs its deployed origin permitted for tile-service CORS. Contact SaanSeoi before launch if your origin is not already allowed. A browser
tiles_getting_started_security_note_afte: header is not authentication; the bearer token is.
get_started_meta_description: Create an account and API key to use the Saanseoi APIs responsibly.
get_started_description: Saanseoi APIs make carefully maintained Hong Kong data easier to use. Create an account, generate an API key, and use it for every request.
get_started_key_description: API keys identify the application making a request. They let us protect the service, understand demand, and contact you if there is a problem.
get_started_step_one_body: Use a single account to manage access across the Saanseoi APIs.
get_started_step_two_body: Give each application its own key so access can be managed without interrupting your other work.
get_started_step_three_body: Include your key in the x-api-key header when calling an API endpoint.
get_started_fair_use_heading: Keep the service available to everyone.
get_started_fair_use_body_one: The APIs are shared public infrastructure. Use caching, request only the data you need, and avoid automated traffic that places an unreasonable load on the service.
get_started_fair_use_body_two: Do not share keys, embed them in public client-side applications, or use them to bypass published limits. Keys may be rate-limited, suspended, or revoked when necessary to keep the service reliable and equitable.
get_started_ready_description: Account and API-key management will be available from your dashboard.

themes_hero: Choose a visual language for your map.
themes_description: Compare SaanSeoi-ready Protomaps styles across Hong Kong, Macao and the Greater Bay Area.
themes_what_is_body: A map style is JSON instructions for a map renderer. It decides which source layers appear, the order they draw in, and the colours, lines, labels and symbols people see. It does not contain the map data itself.
themes_protomaps_body: SaanSeoi’s XXX layer schema targets Protomaps, so these styles use Protomaps’ style system. Start with a flavour, add your SaanSeoi vector source as basemap, then extend it programmatically when your map needs something particular.
themes_preview_landmark: The previews use a familiar local landmark at both zooms.

guide_zed_setup_intro: Let's set you up with a full-fledged AI-powered programming environment!
guide_zed_setup_alternative: If these steps or the result feel too complex, consider getting a VPN and signing up for OpenAI Codex or Claude Cowork instead. Their apps offer an easier onboarding process.
guide_zed_setup_without_vpn: To get Agentic AI in Hong Kong without using a VPN, we’ll use Zed (a code editor) and get acces to models through OpenRouter (a centralised access point to many LLM offerings).
guide_zed_setup_step_install_description: Download Zed; install, and open it.
guide_zed_setup_account_description: Sign up for OpenRouter with Google, GitHub or your email address.
guide_zed_setup_account_confirmation: Confirm your email if they ask you to.
guide_zed_setup_credit_description: Click Add credits on OpenRouter’s Credits Page.
guide_zed_setup_credit_note: Add a payment method and top up US$5. That will cover this guide and then some.
guide_zed_setup_key_description: Head over to the OpenRouter keys page and click “New Key”:
guide_zed_setup_key_once: Your new key will be displayed in another dialog. This is the only time you will see this key, so copy it to a safe place.
guide_zed_setup_key_example: Your key will look something like sk-or-v1-…. Treat it like a password.
guide_zed_setup_key_manage: Your key can now be managed from the dashboard. If you accidentally publish it, delete it there so nobody else can drain your credits.
guide_zed_setup_open_zed_description: Open Zed if you haven’t already. If the welcome screen is open, close the tab.
guide_zed_setup_agent_setup_description: If any of these steps are unclear, Zed’s OpenRouter instructions cover adding an OpenRouter model and provide further guidance.
guide_zed_setup_project_description: Click "Open Project" and, if you don't have a project directory yet, create one. We'll use "saanseoi-project" in this guide.
guide_zed_setup_project_add_description: Click "Open" to add the directory as a project to Zed.
guide_zed_setup_trust_description: When Zed asks you to trust the directory, click “Trust and Continue”.
guide_zed_setup_provider_description: Now let's add the Openrouter API Token so ZED can talk to our LLM models. As the name suggests, OpenRouter routes our messages to other LLM providers and routes their response back to us.
guide_zed_setup_provider_docs: Scroll to OpenRouter and paste the key beginning with sk-or-v1- into the provider field. Press Enter. OpenRouter is now configured as a provider in Zed. Settings can be closed.
guide_zed_setup_model_intro: OpenRouter offers thousands of model / provider options — so let’s specify a model that’s the current (AUG 2026) champion in the cost-efficient programming segment. It’ll be more than sufficient for completing this guide and then customising your map beyond that.

guide_llm_quickstart_prompt: Help me make a map with SaanSeoi. Use https://saanseoi.hk/guides/create-a-map as the source of truth and follow its guidance. Before doing any setup, ask me what I want the map to do, who it is for and which dataset I would like to use. If the answer makes a default unsuitable, ask a follow-up question instead of guessing. Otherwise, use these defaults: create a local TypeScript web project with Bun and Vite, use MapLibre to render it, start with the SaanSeoi Hong Kong basemap and Light style, and prepare to add my own data. Once the mapping environment is running, consult me about the data I want to add and the next feature to build. Explain decisions as you go, do not expose credentials, and stop before any action that needs my account credentials.

guide_data_urban_density_description: Build a map that compares urban land in Hong Kong, Kowloon and the New Territories. It overlays the urban land you calculate on the SaanSeoi basemap and puts one large density metric for each region at the bottom of the screen.
guide_data_urban_density_definition: This is an area-based estimate: it divides the combined district population by the urban land area in that region. District statistics do not tell us where people live within a district, so do not present it as the population living inside each individual urban polygon.
guide_data_urban_density_inputs_descript: Use the SaanSeoi district source release for the district geometry, and normalise its identifiers to SaanSeoi district codes. Use one reference year from C&SD’s District Land Area, Population and Density dataset for the population values. Convert every geometry to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) before calculating: Turf’s area function expects geographic coordinates. Export the original, unclipped land-use data that underpins the basemap: vector-tile fragments overlap and repeat at tile edges, so they cannot produce a valid area total.

Review it for your question before publishing: for example, parks, schools and transport land may or may not belong in your definition of urban land. The union prevents overlapping land-use features from being counted twice.

guide_terminal_intro_description:
A terminal is an app for giving direct instructions to your computer. We'll cover enough ground here for you to feel confident using one.

Like with an LLM, you write a prompt — but in the command line (another word for the terminal) it must be a precise command. Your computer then runs exactly what was asked of it.

Programmers love (and often live in!) the terminal because each command does what it says it'll do, making them repeatable, automatable and indeed shareable in guides like these.
guide_terminal_intro_open_windows:
1. Search. Press the Windows key and type Windows Terminal.
  2. Open. Press Enter. Windows Terminal is the app; it opens a PowerShell tab by default.
guide_terminal_intro_open_macos:
1. Search. Press Command + Space and type Terminal.
  2. Open. Press Return.
guide_terminal_intro_open_linux:
1. Search. Open your application launcher and type Terminal.
  2. Open. Select the Terminal app.
guide_terminal_intro_navigation_unix: cd folder-name moves to a folder. ls lists what is in the current folder. Use cd .. to go back up one folder.
guide_terminal_intro_navigation_windows: cd folder-name moves to a folder. dir lists what is in the current folder. Use cd .. to go back up one folder.
guide_terminal_intro_completion: Press Tab to complete a file or folder name when the terminal can work it out.
guide_terminal_intro_history: Press the Up Arrow to bring back the command you ran most recently.
guide_terminal_intro_interrupt: If a command keeps running, press Control + C to stop it and return to the prompt.
guide_terminal_intro_paste_windows: In Windows Terminal, use <kbd>Control</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> or right-click to paste. Check the whole command before you press Enter.
guide_terminal_intro_paste_macos: In Terminal, use <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> to paste. Check the whole command before you press Return.
guide_terminal_intro_paste_linux: In most Linux terminals, use <kbd>Control</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> or right-click to paste. Check the whole command before you press Enter.
guide_terminal_intro_recovery_check: Compare the command. Check every character against the guide before changing anything else.
guide_terminal_intro_recovery_read: Read the output. The first error often points directly to the problem.
guide_terminal_intro_recovery_ask_after: safely. Share the command, all output, your intented outcome, and what happened instead — never include passwords or API keys.
guide_terminal_intro_learn_more: Learn Enough Command Line to Be Dangerous
